title: 思考のトレーニング
subtitle: Training of Thought
educationalGoal: Through learning to summarize arguments, grasp their structure, and evaluate their validity and soundness, students will develop the ability to create and sustain spaces for constructive discussion on their own. The course begins with careful understanding of others’ spoken statements and written texts, and ultimately aims to enable students to develop and present their own original arguments.
advice: First, this course introduces key concepts and methods for structurally understanding and analyzing Japanese texts and spoken discourse. Specifically, students will learn to identify the basic components of sentences-such as negation, conjunction, disjunction, and conditionals-as well as various connective expressions that link sentences and arguments, including interpretation, justification, addition, and contrast. Through this process, students will develop the ability to grasp the structure of arguments. In addition, the course aims to cultivate the ability to evaluate arguments whose structure has been clarified in this way. Particular emphasis is placed on assessing whether an argument is valid. By developing these skills, students will also acquire the ability to raise precise and constructive questions about specific arguments. Ultimately, through analyzing and evaluating the structure of arguments on a given topic, students will learn to construct their own well-reasoned arguments on that topic.
books: 野矢茂樹(2006).『新版 論理トレーニング』、産業図書.

achievementLevels.standard: ・Generally accurately grasp the meaning of texts and the structure of arguments by paying attention to logical and rhetorical connectives. ・Generally accurately evaluate the validity of arguments. ・Formulate generally appropriate and relevant questions regarding a given argument. ・Develop and present one’s own argument on a given topic with general coherence and appropriateness.
